# Portfolio 2 - benchmark results (generated by sql/run_benchmarks.py)

Run started: 2026-11-04 13:21:00

## Test environment

- Server: MariaDB 10.4.32-MariaDB (XAMPP), storage engine InnoDB, isolation REPEATABLE-READ
- InnoDB buffer pool: 16 MB (XAMPP default, not changed); redo log file: 5 MB
- Host: Windows-11-10.0.26200-SP0, Python 3.14.3
- Data: synthetic bulk data from `01_generate_bulk_data.sql` (fixed random seeds)
- E5 test pair: source account 1001 -> destination 1045 (1 matching transfer(s))
- Table sizes at test time:

| table | est. rows | data MB | index MB |
|---|---|---|---|
| accounts | 79989 | 5.5 | 5.0 |
| audit_log | 160173 | 10.5 | 6.5 |
| beneficiaries | 5 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| customers | 49956 | 4.5 | 6.0 |
| transactions | 777829 | 43.6 | 37.1 |
| transfers | 110038 | 8.5 | 20.6 |

## Method

- Each variant is run 6 times. Times are server-side `r_total_time_ms` from `ANALYZE FORMAT=JSON`. **First run** = first execution after the index change (data may need reading from disk); **median of repeats** = median of runs 2-6 (data mostly cached).
- **Rows read** = sum of `Handler_read_*` counters for one execution. It does not depend on machine load, so it is the most reliable comparison.
- For covering (index-only) plans, index entries still count as rows read, but the lookups into the table are skipped, so the time difference is the better indicator there.
- `EXPLAIN` = estimated plan (query not run). `ANALYZE` = actual plan with measured `r_rows`. Raw outputs are in `execution-plans/`.
- The laptop was in normal use during the runs, so small timing differences are noise; large differences and the rows-read counts are what matter.

## Results

### E1 - Account lookup by account number

Point lookup. The Portfolio 1 schema has a UNIQUE index on account_number; the baseline drops it for the test.

| variant | plan (EXPLAIN) | rows read | first run ms | median repeat ms | index build s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (no index on account_number) | accounts: type=ALL, key=NULL, est.rows=79989, Using where | 80,010 | 103.9 | 68.0 | 0.06 |
| optimised (UNIQUE index on account_number restored) | accounts: type=const, key=uq_accounts_number, est.rows=1 | 1 | 0.005 | 0.003 | 0.29 |

Rows read: 80,010 -> 1 (80010.0x fewer). Median repeat time: 68.0 ms -> 0.003 ms (at least one is under 0.5 ms, too small for a meaningful ratio).

### E2 - Account statement: latest 20 transactions of a busy account

Baseline has only a single-column index on account_id (what indexing "just the foreign key" gives). The composite index (account_id, created_at) lets MariaDB read the newest rows in order and stop after 20.

| variant | plan (EXPLAIN) | rows read | first run ms | median repeat ms | index build s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (index on account_id only) | transactions: type=ref, key=idx_tmp_account, est.rows=2218, Using where; Using filesort | 2,219 | 441.4 | 216.5 | 1.6 |
| optimised (composite index (account_id, created_at)) | transactions: type=ref, key=idx_transactions_account_created, est.rows=2218, Using where | 20 | 4.8 | 0.157 | 1.66 |

Rows read: 2,219 -> 20 (111.0x fewer). Median repeat time: 216.5 ms -> 0.157 ms (at least one is under 0.5 ms, too small for a meaningful ratio).

### E3 - Monthly volume report (range filter + aggregate)

transactions has no index on created_at in the Portfolio 1 schema, so the baseline scans the whole ledger. The optimised variant adds a covering index, so the query is answered from the index alone.

| variant | plan (EXPLAIN) | rows read | first run ms | median repeat ms | index build s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (no index that starts with created_at) | transactions: type=ALL, key=NULL, est.rows=779204, Using where; Using temporary; Using filesort | 812,758 | 461.9 | 571.0 | - |
| optimised (covering index (created_at, transaction_type, amount)) | transactions: type=range, key=idx_transactions_created_cover, est.rows=60992, Using where; Using index; Using temporary; Using filesort | 65,466 | 81.8 | 59.3 | 1.91 |

Rows read: 812,758 -> 65,466 (12.4x fewer). Median repeat time: 571.0 ms -> 59.3 ms (9.6x).

### E4 - Single-day report: wrapping the column in a function vs a range

Same index in both variants (created_at). Only the query text changes. DATE(created_at) = ... hides the column from the index; the range form lets it be used.

| variant | plan (EXPLAIN) | rows read | first run ms | median repeat ms | index build s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (WHERE DATE(created_at) = '2026-03-15') | transactions: type=ALL, key=NULL, est.rows=778516, Using where | 780,021 | 560.4 | 502.4 | 1.42 |
| optimised (range: created_at >= '2026-03-15' AND created_at < '2026-03-16') | transactions: type=range, key=idx_tmp_created, est.rows=1094, Using index condition | 1,095 | 5.0 | 2.4 | - |

Rows read: 780,021 -> 1,095 (712.3x fewer). Median repeat time: 502.4 ms -> 2.4 ms (211.2x).

### E5 - Transfers between a specific pair of accounts

Hypothesis: a composite index on the (source, destination) pair beats the Portfolio 1 indexes, because (source_account_id, created_at) would have to read every transfer from the busy source account. This experiment tests that hypothesis; the result is reported as measured.

| variant | plan (EXPLAIN) | rows read | first run ms | median repeat ms | index build s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (Portfolio 1 indexes only) | transfers: type=ref, key=idx_transfers_destination, est.rows=3, Using where | 4 | 0.691 | 0.081 | - |
| optimised (new index (source_account_id, destination_account_id)) | transfers: type=ref, key=idx_transfers_pair, est.rows=1 | 2 | 0.518 | 0.043 | 0.33 |

Rows read: 4 -> 2 (2.0x fewer). Median repeat time: 0.081 ms -> 0.043 ms (at least one is under 0.5 ms, too small for a meaningful ratio).

### E6 - Top 10 senders by completed transfer value in Q1 2026 (join + aggregate)

The Portfolio 1 index (status, created_at) finds the right transfers but must fetch each row for source_account_id and amount. The optimised covering index holds every column the query needs.

| variant | plan (EXPLAIN) | rows read | first run ms | median repeat ms | index build s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (existing index (status, created_at)) | t: type=ref, key=idx_transfers_status_created, est.rows=55019, Using index condition; Using where; Using temporary; Using filesort<br>a: type=eq_ref, key=PRIMARY, est.rows=1 | 52,366 | 745.2 | 480.3 | - |
| optimised (covering index (status, created_at, source_account_id, amount)) | t: type=range, key=idx_transfers_status_created_cover, est.rows=25340, Using where; Using index; Using temporary; Using filesort<br>a: type=eq_ref, key=PRIMARY, est.rows=1 | 52,366 | 289.8 | 51.9 | 0.36 |

Rows read: 52,366 -> 52,366 (about the same). Median repeat time: 480.3 ms -> 51.9 ms (9.2x).
